name: Organic Chemistry
description: The study of the structure, properties, reactions, and synthesis of carbon-based compounds.

name: Inorganic Chemistry
description: The study of the structure, properties, and reactions of elements and compounds that are not carbon-organic, spanning metals, minerals, and coordination complexes.

name: Physical Chemistry
description: The branch applying physics concepts to explain chemical systems, including thermodynamics, kinetics, and quantum behavior.

name: Analytical Chemistry
description: The science of separating, identifying, and quantifying the chemical components of matter.

name: Biochemistry
description: The study of chemical processes and molecules within and relating to living organisms.

name: Theoretical Chemistry
description: The development of mathematical and computational models to describe chemical structure, bonding, and reactivity.

name: Polymer Chemistry
description: The study of the synthesis, structure, and properties of macromolecules and polymers.

name: Nuclear Chemistry
description: The study of radioactive elements, nuclear transformations, and the chemical effects of radiation.

name: Medicinal Chemistry
description: The chemistry discipline devoted to the design, synthesis, and optimization of pharmaceutical agents.

name: Food Chemistry
description: The study of the chemical composition, reactions, and transformations of food during processing and storage.

name: Environmental Chemistry
description: The study of chemical phenomena in natural environments and the fate of pollutants in air, water, and soil.

name: Materials Chemistry
description: The chemistry-driven design, synthesis, and understanding of solid and functional materials.

name: Alchemy
description: The historical proto-scientific practice combining metallurgy, mysticism, and early chemistry in pursuit of metal transmutation and an elixir of life.

name: Chinese Alchemy
description: The Taoist-influenced Chinese proto-chemical tradition seeking elixirs of immortality, which contributed to early gunpowder and pharmaceutical chemistry.

name: Organic Reaction Mechanisms
description: The study of the step-by-step pathways by which organic reactions proceed at the molecular level.

name: Stereochemistry
description: The study of the three-dimensional spatial arrangement of atoms in molecules and its effect on reactivity.

name: Organic Synthesis
description: The construction of organic compounds through planned sequences of chemical reactions.

name: Total Synthesis
description: The complete laboratory construction of complex natural products from simple starting materials.

name: Retrosynthetic Analysis
description: A problem-solving strategy that works backward from a target molecule to identify simpler precursor structures.

name: Asymmetric Synthesis
description: The selective preparation of one enantiomer or diastereomer of a chiral molecule.

name: Organocatalysis
description: The acceleration of reactions using small organic molecules as catalysts instead of metals or enzymes.

name: Heterocyclic Chemistry
description: The chemistry of ring compounds containing heteroatoms such as nitrogen, oxygen, or sulfur.

name: Natural Product Chemistry
description: The isolation, characterization, and synthesis of chemical compounds produced by living organisms.

name: Carbohydrate Chemistry
description: The study of the structure, synthesis, and reactions of sugars and polysaccharides.

name: Organic Photochemistry
description: The study of light-induced chemical reactions of organic molecules.

name: Physical Organic Chemistry
description: The quantitative study of the relationship between organic molecular structure and reactivity using physical principles.

name: Supramolecular Chemistry
description: The chemistry of non-covalent interactions and the assemblies of multiple molecules into larger structures.

name: Coordination Chemistry
description: The study of compounds in which metal centers are bound to surrounding ligands.

name: Crystal Field Theory
description: A model describing the electronic structure and colors of transition-metal complexes via ligand-induced splitting of d-orbitals.

name: Ligand Field Theory
description: An extension of crystal field theory incorporating covalent metal-ligand bonding into molecular orbital descriptions.

name: Organometallic Chemistry
description: The study of compounds containing direct metal-carbon bonds.

name: Bioinorganic Chemistry
description: The study of the roles of metals and metalloenzymes in biological systems.

name: Solid State Chemistry
description: The synthesis, structure, and properties of solid-phase materials and their phase behavior.

name: Main Group Chemistry
description: The chemistry of the s- and p-block elements of the periodic table.

name: Transition Metal Chemistry
description: The chemistry of the d-block elements and their characteristic variable oxidation states and complexes.

name: Lanthanide and Actinide Chemistry
description: The chemistry of the rare-earth lanthanide and radioactive actinide elements.

name: Metal Cluster Chemistry
description: The study of compounds in which multiple metal atoms are directly bonded into clusters.

name: Chemical Thermodynamics
description: The study of energy, entropy, and spontaneity in chemical reactions and phase changes.

name: Thermochemistry
description: The measurement and interpretation of heat changes accompanying chemical processes.

name: Chemical Equilibrium
description: The state of a reversible reaction in which forward and reverse rates balance and concentrations stabilize.

name: Solution Thermodynamics
description: The thermodynamics of mixing, solvation, and non-ideal behavior in solutions.

name: Chemical Kinetics
description: The study of reaction rates, rate laws, and the mechanisms controlling them.

name: Reaction Dynamics
description: The detailed study of how energy and molecular collisions determine reaction pathways.

name: Catalysis
description: The acceleration of chemical reactions by substances that are not consumed in the process.

name: Homogeneous Catalysis
description: Catalysis in which the catalyst and reactants share a single phase, typically solution.

name: Heterogeneous Catalysis
description: Catalysis occurring at the surface of a solid catalyst in a different phase from the reactants.

name: Photocatalysis
description: Catalysis driven by light-absorbing materials that generate reactive species at surfaces.

name: Electrochemistry
description: The study of the interconversion of chemical and electrical energy at electrodes and in ionic conductors.

name: Battery Chemistry
description: The chemistry of charge storage, electrode materials, and electrolytes in electrochemical cells.

name: Statistical Mechanics
description: The bridge from microscopic molecular behavior to macroscopic thermodynamic properties via ensemble averages.

name: Surface Chemistry
description: The study of physical and chemical phenomena at the interfaces of phases, including adsorption.

name: Colloid and Interface Chemistry
description: The study of dispersed systems such as emulsions, foams, and suspensions with large interfacial area.

name: Photochemistry
description: The study of chemical reactions initiated or mediated by the absorption of light.

name: Quantum Chemistry
description: The application of quantum mechanics to molecular structure, bonding, and electronic spectra.

name: Molecular Orbital Theory
description: A quantum model describing bonding in terms of delocalized molecular orbitals formed from atomic orbitals.

name: Valence Bond Theory
description: A quantum model describing bonding in terms of localized overlapping atomic orbitals and resonance.

name: Computational Chemistry
description: The use of computer simulation and numerical methods to model chemical systems and predict properties.

name: Ab Initio Methods
description: Quantum chemical calculations derived from first principles without empirical parameters.

name: Density Functional Theory
description: A widely used quantum method computing electronic structure from the electron density distribution.

name: Semiempirical Methods
description: Approximate quantum calculations that incorporate experimental parameters to reduce computational cost.

name: Molecular Mechanics
description: Classical force-field models of molecular geometry and energy that ignore electronic motion.

name: Molecular Dynamics
description: Simulation of the time evolution of molecular systems by integrating classical equations of motion.

name: Monte Carlo Simulation
description: Stochastic sampling methods for computing thermodynamic averages of molecular systems.

name: Cheminformatics
description: The use of computational and information techniques to store, retrieve, and analyze chemical data.

name: Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship
description: Statistical models relating molecular structure descriptors to biological or chemical activity.

name: Mathematical Chemistry
description: The application of mathematics, especially graph theory, to chemical structure and properties.

name: Chemical Graph Theory
description: The representation of molecules as graphs to study topology, isomerism, and molecular descriptors.

name: Polymer Synthesis
description: The methods by which monomers are linked into high-molecular-weight polymer chains.

name: Step-Growth Polymerization
description: Polymerization in which multifunctional monomers react stepwise, as in polyesters and polyamides.

name: Chain-Growth Polymerization
description: Polymerization that proceeds by reactive-center propagation along a growing chain.

name: Radical Polymerization
description: Chain-growth polymerization propagated by free-radical intermediates.

name: Ionic Polymerization
description: Chain-growth polymerization propagated by cationic or anionic active centers.

name: Coordination Polymerization
description: Polymerization mediated by transition-metal catalysts that control stereochemistry, as in Ziegler-Natta catalysis.

name: Ring-Opening Polymerization
description: Polymerization initiated by opening cyclic monomers such as lactones and epoxides.

name: Polymer Characterization
description: The measurement of molecular weight, structure, and thermal and mechanical properties of polymers.

name: Polymer Physics
description: The physical theory of polymer conformations, elasticity, and viscoelasticity.

name: Biopolymers
description: Naturally occurring macromolecules such as proteins, nucleic acids, and polysaccharides.

name: Conductive Polymers
description: Organic polymers that conduct electricity through conjugated backbones and doping.

name: Polymer Rheology
description: The study of the flow and deformation behavior of polymer melts and solutions.

name: Radiochemistry
description: The chemistry of radioactive isotopes, their preparation, separation, and measurement.

name: Radiation Chemistry
description: The study of chemical effects produced by ionizing radiation on matter.

name: Isotope Chemistry
description: The study of the chemical behavior and separation of isotopes of the elements.

name: Actinide Chemistry
description: The chemistry of the radioactive actinide series, including uranium, plutonium, and transuranics.

name: Radioanalytical Chemistry
description: Analytical techniques using radioactivity and nuclear properties to measure trace species.

name: Nuclear Forensics
description: The analysis of nuclear and radioactive materials to determine their origin, history, and intended use.

name: Qualitative Analysis
description: The identification of which chemical species are present in a sample.

name: Quantitative Analysis
description: The determination of the amount or concentration of chemical species in a sample.

name: Gravimetric Analysis
description: Quantification by measuring the mass of a purified analyte or its precipitate.

name: Titrimetry
description: Volumetric quantification by reacting an analyte with a reagent of known concentration to an endpoint.

name: Instrumental Analysis
description: Analysis performed with electronic instruments measuring physical properties of analytes.

name: Spectroscopy
description: The measurement of the interaction of electromagnetic radiation with matter to identify and quantify species.

name: Atomic Spectroscopy
description: Spectroscopic techniques that analyze free atoms in the gas phase.

name: Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy
description: Quantification of elements by measuring light absorbed by ground-state atoms.

name: Atomic Emission Spectroscopy
description: Quantification of elements by measuring light emitted from excited atoms in a plasma or flame.

name: Molecular Spectroscopy
description: Spectroscopic study of molecules through their rotational, vibrational, and electronic transitions.

name: UV-Visible Spectroscopy
description: Absorption spectroscopy in the ultraviolet-visible region probing electronic transitions.

name: Infrared Spectroscopy
description: Absorption spectroscopy in the infrared region probing molecular vibrations and functional groups.

name: Raman Spectroscopy
description: Inelastic light scattering spectroscopy probing vibrational modes complementary to infrared absorption.

name: Fluorescence Spectroscopy
description: Emission spectroscopy of light released as excited molecules relax, used for sensitive detection.

name: NMR Spectroscopy
description: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy resolving molecular structure via nuclear spin transitions in magnetic fields.

name: Mass Spectrometry
description: The measurement of the mass-to-charge ratios of ionized molecules for identification and quantification.

name: Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry
description: Hyphenated separation and identification of volatile compounds by gas chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry.

name: Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry
description: Separation and identification of non-volatile and polar analytes by liquid chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry.

name: Tandem Mass Spectrometry
description: Multiple-stage mass spectrometry in which selected ions are fragmented for structural elucidation.

name: Chromatography
description: Separation of mixtures by differential partitioning between a stationary and a mobile phase.

name: Gas Chromatography
description: Separation of volatile compounds in a gaseous mobile phase through a coated capillary column.

name: Liquid Chromatography
description: Separation of analytes in a liquid mobile phase passed through a packed column.

name: High-Performance Liquid Chromatography
description: High-pressure liquid chromatography providing rapid, high-resolution separation of complex mixtures.

name: Thin-Layer Chromatography
description: Planar chromatography on a coated plate used for rapid qualitative screening.

name: Ion Chromatography
description: Separation and quantification of ions using ion-exchange stationary phases and conductivity detection.

name: Size-Exclusion Chromatography
description: Separation of macromolecules by molecular size through a porous gel matrix.

name: Electroanalytical Methods
description: Analytical techniques based on the electrical response of analyte solutions at electrodes.

name: Potentiometry
description: Measurement of electrode potential to determine analyte concentration, as in pH electrodes.

name: Voltammetry
description: Measurement of current as a function of applied potential for trace analysis of electroactive species.

name: Coulometry
description: Quantification by measuring the total charge passed during complete electrolysis of an analyte.

name: Thermal Analysis
description: Measurement of material properties as a function of temperature.

name: Differential Scanning Calorimetry
description: Measurement of heat flow into a sample to characterize phase transitions and thermal stability.

name: Thermogravimetric Analysis
description: Measurement of mass change with temperature to study decomposition and volatilization.

name: Separation Science
description: The systematic study and development of methods to resolve mixtures into pure components.

name: Sample Preparation
description: Techniques for extracting, concentrating, and cleaning samples before instrumental analysis.

name: Chemometrics
description: The application of statistical and mathematical methods to chemical measurement and data.

name: Bioanalytical Chemistry
description: Analytical methods for measuring molecules in biological matrices such as blood and tissue.

name: Drug Design
description: The rational design of new therapeutic molecules based on biological target structure.

name: Computer-Aided Drug Design
description: Computational methods for discovering and optimizing drug candidates, including docking and virtual screening.

name: Pharmacokinetics
description: The quantitative study of drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion over time.

name: Drug Metabolism
description: The biochemical transformation of drugs in the body, largely by liver enzymes.

name: Combinatorial Chemistry
description: The rapid synthesis of large libraries of related compounds for screening.

name: Peptide Therapeutics
description: The design and chemistry of peptide-based drugs and their stabilization for clinical use.

name: Flavor Chemistry
description: The study of the volatile and non-volatile compounds responsible for food aroma and taste.

name: Food Analysis
description: Analytical determination of nutrients, contaminants, and additives in food products.

name: Food Additives
description: Chemical substances added to foods to preserve, color, sweeten, or stabilize them.

name: Nutraceuticals
description: Food-derived compounds with physiological or medicinal benefits beyond basic nutrition.

name: Food Biochemistry
description: The biochemical reactions of enzymes and nutrients during food production and storage.

name: Aquatic Chemistry
description: The chemistry of natural waters, including speciation, redox, and acid-base equilibria.

name: Green Chemistry
description: The design of chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate hazardous substances.

name: Environmental Analysis
description: Analytical measurement of pollutants and trace chemicals in environmental media.

name: Nanochemistry
description: The chemical synthesis and study of materials at the nanoscale.

name: Crystal Engineering
description: The design of crystalline solids with desired properties by controlling intermolecular interactions.

name: Metal-Organic Frameworks
description: Porous crystalline materials built from metal nodes and organic linkers, used for storage and separation.

name: Zeolite Chemistry
description: The chemistry of microporous aluminosilicate minerals used as catalysts and adsorbents.

name: Molecular Biology
description: The study of biological processes at the molecular level, focusing on nucleic acids, proteins, and their interactions.

name: Cell Biology
description: The study of cell structure, function, and the processes governing cellular life.

name: Genetics
description: The study of genes, heredity, and genetic variation in organisms.

name: Evolutionary Biology
description: The study of the evolutionary processes that produce the diversity of life.

name: Ecology
description: The study of the interactions between organisms and their environments.

name: Microbiology
description: The study of microorganisms including bacteria, viruses, fungi, and protists.

name: Botany
description: The scientific study of plants, including their structure, physiology, classification, and ecology.

name: Zoology
description: The scientific study of animals, including their anatomy, behavior, classification, and evolution.

name: Physiology
description: The study of the functions and mechanisms of living organisms and their organ systems.

name: Immunology
description: The study of the immune system and its defense against pathogens and disease.

name: Developmental Biology
description: The study of how organisms grow and develop from a single cell to mature form.

name: Structural Biology
description: The determination and study of the three-dimensional structures of biological macromolecules.

name: Systems Biology
description: The holistic computational and mathematical study of complex biological systems and networks.

name: Synthetic Biology
description: The design and construction of new biological parts, systems, and organisms.

name: Chronobiology
description: The study of biological rhythms and their timing mechanisms.

name: Marine Biology
description: The study of organisms living in marine and estuarine environments.

name: Conservation Biology
description: The science of protecting and restoring biodiversity and threatened species.

name: Biophysics
description: The application of physics principles and methods to biological systems.

name: Anatomy
description: The study of the structure and organization of organisms and their parts.

name: DNA Replication
description: The process by which a cell copies its DNA prior to cell division.

name: DNA Repair
description: The cellular mechanisms that correct damage to DNA molecules.

name: DNA Recombination
description: The exchange and rearrangement of DNA sequences between molecules.

name: Transcription
description: The synthesis of RNA from a DNA template.

name: RNA Splicing
description: The removal of introns and joining of exons in precursor messenger RNA.

name: RNA Processing
description: Post-transcriptional modifications that convert primary transcripts into functional RNA.

name: Translation
description: The synthesis of proteins from messenger RNA templates on ribosomes.

name: Gene Expression Regulation
description: The control of when, where, and how much genes are expressed.

name: Epigenetics
description: Heritable changes in gene expression that do not involve changes to the DNA sequence.

name: DNA Methylation
description: The addition of methyl groups to DNA, typically silencing gene expression.

name: Histone Modification
description: Post-translational chemical changes to histone proteins that regulate chromatin structure.

name: Chromatin Biology
description: The study of chromatin structure and its role in genome organization and regulation.

name: RNA Biology
description: The study of the structure, function, and regulation of RNA molecules.

name: Non-Coding RNA
description: Functional RNA molecules that are not translated into protein.

name: Transcriptomics
description: The genome-wide study of RNA transcripts and their expression levels.

name: Proteomics
description: The large-scale study of the structure, function, and interactions of proteins.

name: Metabolomics
description: The comprehensive study of small-molecule metabolites within cells and organisms.

name: Membrane Biology
description: The study of the structure and function of biological membranes.

name: Cell Signaling
description: The molecular mechanisms by which cells detect and respond to extracellular signals.

name: Cell Cycle
description: The series of events by which a cell grows, replicates its DNA, and divides.

name: Cell Division
description: The processes of mitosis and meiosis by which cells reproduce.

name: Apoptosis
description: Programmed cell death that eliminates damaged or unneeded cells.

name: Stem Cell Biology
description: The study of undifferentiated cells capable of self-renewal and differentiation.

name: Cell Adhesion
description: The study of how cells bind to one another and to the extracellular matrix.

name: Cell Motility
description: The study of how cells move and migrate in response to cues.

name: Cytoskeleton Biology
description: The study of the cytoskeletal filaments that provide cell shape, support, and transport.

name: Organelle Biology
description: The study of membrane-bound cellular compartments and their functions.

name: Mitochondrial Biology
description: The study of mitochondria, their genetics, energy production, and dysfunction.

name: Autophagy
description: The cellular process of degrading and recycling damaged organelles and proteins.

name: Mendelian Genetics
description: The classical study of inheritance patterns described by Gregor Mendel's laws.

name: Molecular Genetics
description: The study of the molecular structure and function of genes.

name: Cytogenetics
description: The study of chromosomes and their role in heredity and disease.

name: Population Genetics
description: The study of allele frequency distributions and their change within populations.

name: Quantitative Genetics
description: The statistical study of continuously varying traits and their genetic architecture.

name: Genomics
description: The study of entire genomes, their structure, function, and evolution.

name: Structural Genomics
description: The determination of the three-dimensional structures of genome-encoded proteins at scale.

name: Functional Genomics
description: The genome-wide analysis of gene function and regulation.

name: Comparative Genomics
description: The comparison of genome sequences across species to identify conserved and divergent elements.

name: Metagenomics
description: The direct study of genetic material recovered from environmental samples.

name: Shotgun Metagenomics
description: Untargeted sequencing of all DNA in an environmental sample to profile community composition and function.

name: Single-Cell Genomics
description: Genomic and transcriptomic analysis at the resolution of individual cells.

name: Epigenomics
description: The genome-wide study of epigenetic modifications and chromatin states.

name: Human Genetics
description: The study of inheritance and genetic variation in human populations.

name: Medical Genetics
description: The application of genetics to the diagnosis and management of inherited disease.

name: Behavioral Genetics
description: The study of genetic contributions to behavior and psychological traits.

name: Immunogenetics
description: The genetics of the immune system, including HLA and antibody diversity.

name: Pharmacogenomics
description: The study of how genetic variation affects individual drug response.

name: Developmental Genetics
description: The genetic control of developmental processes and pattern formation.

name: Molecular Evolution
description: The study of evolutionary change at the level of DNA and protein sequences.

name: Phylogenetics
description: The inference of evolutionary relationships among organisms or genes.

name: Cladistics
description: A classification method grouping organisms by shared derived characteristics.

name: Speciation
description: The evolutionary process by which new biological species arise.

name: Macroevolution
description: Evolutionary change at and above the species level over geological time.

name: Microevolution
description: Small-scale evolutionary change in allele frequencies within populations.

name: Evolutionary Developmental Biology
description: The comparative study of development to understand how it evolves, also called evo-devo.

name: Coevolution
description: Reciprocal evolutionary change between interacting species.

name: Sexual Selection
description: Natural selection arising from mate choice and competition for reproduction.

name: Evolutionary Ecology
description: The study of ecology in the light of evolutionary adaptation and fitness.

name: Human Evolution
description: The evolutionary origins and diversification of the human lineage.

name: Population Ecology
description: The study of population size, growth, and dynamics over time.

name: Community Ecology
description: The study of the interactions and assembly of species within ecological communities.

name: Ecosystem Ecology
description: The study of energy flow and nutrient cycling through ecosystems.

name: Landscape Ecology
description: The study of spatial patterns and their ecological effects across heterogeneous landscapes.

name: Behavioral Ecology
description: The evolutionary study of animal behavior in relation to ecological context.

name: Ecophysiology
description: The study of physiological adaptations of organisms to their environments.

name: Molecular Ecology
description: The application of molecular markers to ecological and evolutionary questions.

name: Microbial Ecology
description: The study of microorganisms in their natural environments and their ecological roles.

name: Global Ecology
description: The study of ecological patterns and processes at planetary scale.

name: Restoration Ecology
description: The science of assisting the recovery of degraded or destroyed ecosystems.

name: Urban Ecology
description: The study of ecological systems within cities and urbanizing landscapes.

name: Chemical Ecology
description: The study of chemical signals mediating interactions among organisms.

name: Trophic Ecology
description: The study of feeding relationships and food webs in ecosystems.

name: Agroecology
description: The ecological study of agricultural systems and their sustainability.

name: Biogeography
description: The study of the geographic distribution of species and ecosystems.

name: Island Biogeography
description: The study of species richness and dynamics on islands and isolated habitats.

name: Phylogeography
description: The study of historical processes shaping the geographic distribution of genetic lineages.

name: Traditional Ecological Knowledge
description: Place-based indigenous and local knowledge of ecosystems, species, and sustainable resource use.

name: Bacteriology
description: The study of bacteria and their biology, ecology, and pathogenesis.

name: Virology
description: The study of viruses, their structure, replication, and disease.

name: Mycology
description: The study of fungi, including yeasts, molds, and mushrooms.

name: Parasitology
description: The study of parasitic organisms and their interactions with hosts.

name: Protozoology
description: The study of protozoa, single-celled eukaryotic organisms.

name: Phycology
description: The study of algae, including microscopic phytoplankton and seaweeds.

name: Microbial Physiology
description: The study of the metabolism and functioning of microorganisms.

name: Microbial Genetics
description: The study of genes, heredity, and horizontal transfer in microorganisms.

name: Medical Microbiology
description: The study of microorganisms that cause human disease and their diagnosis.

name: Environmental Microbiology
description: The study of microbial communities and processes in natural environments.

name: Industrial Microbiology
description: The use of microorganisms in industrial production, fermentation, and biotechnology.

name: Food Microbiology
description: The study of microorganisms in food spoilage, safety, and fermentation.

name: Microbial Taxonomy
description: The classification and identification of microorganisms.

name: Plant Anatomy
description: The study of the internal structure and tissues of plants.

name: Plant Morphology
description: The study of the external form and structure of plants.

name: Plant Physiology
description: The study of plant function, including photosynthesis, transport, and growth.

name: Plant Hormone Biology
description: The study of phytohormones that regulate plant growth and development.

name: Plant Nutrition
description: The study of nutrient uptake, transport, and assimilation in plants.

name: Plant Taxonomy
description: The classification, naming, and identification of plants.

name: Plant Genetics
description: The study of genes, heredity, and breeding in plants.

name: Plant Pathology
description: The study of plant diseases and their causative agents.

name: Ethnobotany
description: The study of how human cultures use plants for medicine, food, and materials.

name: Bryology
description: The study of mosses, liverworts, and hornworts.

name: Pteridology
description: The study of ferns and related vascular plants.

name: Dendrology
description: The study of woody plants, especially trees and shrubs.

name: Plant Ecology
description: The study of the distribution and interactions of plants in their environments.

name: Animal Anatomy
description: The study of the structure of animal bodies and organs.

name: Animal Physiology
description: The study of the functions of animal organ systems and processes.

name: Ethology
description: The scientific study of animal behavior in natural conditions.

name: Mammalogy
description: The study of mammals and their biology.

name: Ornithology
description: The study of birds and their biology and ecology.

name: Herpetology
description: The study of amphibians and reptiles.

name: Ichthyology
description: The study of fishes.

name: Entomology
description: The study of insects.

name: Malacology
description: The study of mollusks, including snails, clams, and cephalopods.

name: Arachnology
description: The study of spiders, scorpions, and related arachnids.

name: Nematology
description: The study of nematode roundworms.

name: Primatology
description: The study of primates, including their behavior, ecology, and evolution.

name: Carcinology
description: The study of crustaceans.

name: Animal Taxonomy
description: The classification, naming, and identification of animals.

name: Zoogeography
description: The study of the geographic distribution of animal species.

name: Neurophysiology
description: The study of the function of the nervous system.

name: Cardiovascular Physiology
description: The study of heart and blood vessel function.

name: Respiratory Physiology
description: The study of breathing and gas exchange function.

name: Renal Physiology
description: The study of kidney function and fluid balance.

name: Gastrointestinal Physiology
description: The study of digestive system function.

name: Endocrinology
description: The study of hormones and the endocrine system.

name: Reproductive Physiology
description: The study of reproductive system function and fertility.

name: Muscle Physiology
description: The study of muscle contraction and function.

name: Exercise Physiology
description: The study of the body's acute and chronic responses to exercise.

name: Comparative Physiology
description: The comparative study of physiological function across species.

name: Innate Immunity
description: The non-specific first-line immune defenses present from birth.

name: Adaptive Immunity
description: The antigen-specific immune memory mediated by lymphocytes.

name: Humoral Immunity
description: Antibody-mediated immunity carried out by B cells.

name: Cell-Mediated Immunity
description: Immune responses carried out by T cells against infected cells.

name: Clinical Immunology
description: The medical study of immune disorders and immune-mediated disease.

name: Immunotherapy
description: The treatment of disease by modulating the immune system.

name: Vaccinology
description: The science of vaccine development and immunization.

name: Mucosal Immunology
description: The study of immune responses at mucosal surfaces.

name: Neuroimmunology
description: The study of interactions between the nervous and immune systems.

name: Immunopathology
description: The study of tissue damage caused by immune responses.

name: Embryology
description: The study of embryonic development from fertilization to birth.

name: Morphogenesis
description: The biological processes that shape the form of organisms.

name: Organogenesis
description: The formation and development of organs during embryogenesis.

name: Cell Differentiation
description: The process by which cells become specialized in structure and function.

name: Regeneration Biology
description: The study of how organisms regrow lost tissues and organs.

name: Teratology
description: The study of abnormal development and congenital malformations.

name: X-Ray Crystallography
description: The determination of macromolecular structure by X-ray diffraction from crystals.

name: Cryo-Electron Microscopy
description: Electron microscopy of flash-frozen samples for near-atomic structure determination.

name: Protein Structure Prediction
description: Computational prediction of protein three-dimensional structure from sequence.

name: Network Biology
description: The study of biological systems as networks of interacting components.

name: Metabolic Network Modeling
description: Computational reconstruction and simulation of metabolic networks.

name: Signaling Network Modeling
description: Modeling of intracellular signaling pathways as dynamic networks.

name: Computational Biology
description: The application of computational and mathematical methods to biological problems.

name: Multi-Omics Integration
description: The combined analysis of genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data.

name: Genetic Circuits
description: Engineered networks of genetic parts that perform logic and control functions in cells.

name: Genome Engineering
description: The targeted modification of genomes using tools such as CRISPR and TALENs.

name: Metabolic Engineering
description: The optimization of cellular metabolic pathways for production of desired compounds.

name: Xenobiology
description: The design of biological systems using non-natural chemistry or alternative genetic codes.

name: Protocell Research
description: The construction and study of minimal cell-like structures to investigate life's origins.

name: Circadian Rhythms
description: Endogenous biological rhythms with a roughly 24-hour period.

name: Chronopharmacology
description: The study of how biological rhythms affect drug action and timing of therapy.

name: Marine Ecology
description: The study of interactions among organisms in marine environments.

name: Coral Reef Ecology
description: The study of coral reef ecosystems and their biodiversity.

name: Deep-Sea Biology
description: The study of organisms living in the deep ocean.

name: Fisheries Biology
description: The biology of exploited fish populations and their management.

name: Conservation Genetics
description: The application of genetics to the preservation of endangered species.

name: Wildlife Management
description: The science of sustaining and regulating wild animal populations.
